controls.note: ControlSurface rotates visibleMesh by rest * AngleAxis(pitch*pitchRange + roll*rollRange + yaw*yawRange, Vector3.right) (ControlSurfaceJob_Math.cs:75); one ControlSurface per transform, its attachedSurface = fus_cockpit. Input signs: ControlsFilter.cs:241 uses pitch * gLimitPositive, so pitch > 0 = pull; Cockpit.Joystick (Cockpit.cs:20) uses Z = -roll*range, so roll > 0 = right. Values below assume those signs (live probe 1 settles them).

gauges.note: No stock aircraft has 3D needle instruments: stock flight data is drawn by the tac-screen UI (BasicFlightInstruments in tacScreen_*.prefab: airspeed/altitude/climb/heading as text, horizon as an image). The only stock component that can turn a transform from a flight value is Cockpit.Throttle (rotation mode, throttle only). The other needles need a runtime component or stay at rest. Each needle/card: local +X = toward the pilot, rest = 12 o'clock; Unity +angle about local +X = clockwise as seen by the pilot; angle = (value - v0) * deg_per_unit.
gauges.texture: b25h_gauges: 8 x 8 cells, cell k at column k % 8, row k // 8 (row 0 at v = 0). Faces: 0 airspeed, 1 attitude bezel, 2 altimeter, 3 heading bezel, 4 vsi, 5 fuel, 6/7 manifold L/R, 8/9 rpm L/R, 10 attitude card (horizon), 11 compass card, 12 oil press, 13 oil temp, 14 cyl temp, 15 hydraulic, 16 flaps, 17 gear; 62 = needle (white, tip at the top of the cell), 63 = short needle. Scales start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise over the sweep in the list.

crew.note: Stock multi-crew aircraft (EW-25 4 crew, FastBomber1 / Darkreach 2, UH-90 2) mark each crew member with a GameObject carrying Pilot.cs + CapsuleCollider whose figure has a helmetCamPoint; Aircraft.pilots[] bails them out one by one (Aircraft.cs:150-230, 500 ms apart without ejection seat) after RpcJettisonCanopy ejects every Canopy in the air (Aircraft.cs:2777). There is no separate exit point: the figure leaves from its own transform. Place one Pilot per crew_*_eye (helmetCamPoint on the eye, as done for the pilot), ejectionSeat = false.

hatches.note: Canopy.cs: CanopyHinge.Animate sets transform.localEulerAngles = right * hingeAngle * openAmount (absolute) -> use hatch_* as the CanopyHinge transform (it rests identity under hatch_*_hinge whose local +X = hinge axis). In flight RpcJettisonCanopy calls Canopy.Eject: set ejectionTransform = hatch_* (gets its own Rigidbody, mass ~15 kg, ejectionCollider = a small box on it); on the ground OpenHinges() swings them to hingeAngle. hingeAngle is the Unity angle about the hinge axis (local +X of the hinge empty); axis_parent_space is also given for B25HBuild DoorHinge-style wiring (parents are unrotated, so parent space = root space).

prop_discs.likely_cause_of_vanishing_props: B25HBuild.DiscMesh maps the WHOLE 0-1 square onto the disc, but the CI-22 blur texture holds the blade blur in the top half and the disc in the bottom half; the disc centre samples the transparent band between them, so with blades hidden (index >= 1) the prop is nearly invisible. Inference from the code and texture, not observed in game.

hardpoints.note: Stock pattern (CAS1): the WeaponManager hardpoint transform IS the pylon object, whose mesh origin is its bottom face (CAS1_pylon1 mesh y 0..0.242). Stock mount tops sit above the hardpoint: RocketPod1_single rail mesh top +0.055, bomb_*_single launchpylon1 top +0.030 (500 lb, cluster) / +0.050 (125/250 lb); internal mounts hang bombs 0.15 m below. So our hardpoints sit on the pylon bottom faces and the stock rails sink 3-5.5 cm into the pylon.

breaks.note: Part split and names unchanged (B25HBuild PartSpec list). Each tear plane is shared by the two parts with identical, complementary jagged skin edges (no gap while intact); behind each edge sits a set-back frame (fuselage) or closed rib (wing) and stringer / spar stubs that reach through the plane into the mating part. Break faces use the existing `structure` material (tiled, UV1) like the stock jet_mechanical submesh; skin damage stays on the paint shader (_HitPoints). No separate damaged meshes are needed (the stock aircraft have none).
